clue.text: Charm will ensure entry!

definitions.meaning: to charm is to delight or bewitch someone
a doorway or way in is what lets you get inside

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to enchant or captivate; as a noun it is a door or gateway through which people go in.

clue.text: Tax being cut

definitions.meaning: a duty levied on goods produced at home
to remove by cutting out, as a surgeon does

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a duty on goods like alcohol; as a verb it means to remove surgically.

clue.text: A bit of muscle is required to lean forward

parts.note: to tend is to incline or lean towards
on means forward, as in move on

explanation.surface: Muscle needed for bending forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough band of tissue linking a muscle to bone.

clue.text: A right that is followed by left shows spirit

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A right turn followed by a left shows boldness.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the airy sprite in Shakespeare's The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy sprite who serves Prospero in The Tempest.

clue.text: City once perhaps holding the record

indicators.note: holding means the rearranged word wraps round the record
perhaps hints that the word may be arranged differently

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A town that once held some sort of record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ONCE into CONE, and 'holding' puts LOG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city on the Rhine in Germany.

clue.text: With this the cook may well prepare fine food

definitions.text: With this the cook may well prepare fine food

parts.words: With this the cook may well prepare fine food
parts.note: fine food suggests gourmet cooking, but here it is food shredded fine, as cheese or nutmeg is by a kitchen tool

explanation.surface: A tribute to the utensil behind a chef's delicacies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine food' reads as haute cuisine; the clue means food made into fine shreds.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool with a rough perforated surface that shreds cheese or vegetables into small pieces.

clue.text: A beast turned up carrying papers to be checked

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed animal holds the papers inside
in a down clue turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a deer is a beast of the forest
the press means newspapers

explanation.surface: An animal that flipped over while carrying newspapers to be inspected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes DEER into REED, and 'carrying' puts PRESS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Restrained or held back, as feelings are suppressed.

clue.text: Jack goes off quietly with it

parts.note: milk turns when it goes off or sours
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A man named Jack slips away silently with something.
explanation.walkthrough: A jack here is a device for rotating a roasting spit; 'Jack' looks like a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting jack, the mechanism or servant that rotated meat over a fire.

clue.text: Ray's more correct when a girl appears

indicators.note: to correct is to put right, so the letters are put into the right order

explanation.surface: Ray gets it more right when a girl turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correct' rearranges RAYS and MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, also that of a herb.

clue.text: Cancel it in error and there'll be a song made

indicators.note: letters set down in error are jumbled, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A careless deletion turns into a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges CANCEL and IT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A canticle is a hymn or chant with a biblical text, sung in church services.

clue.text: The radio officer's place for relaxation on board

definitions.text: The radio officer's place for relaxation on board

parts.words: The radio officer's place for relaxation on board
parts.note: on a ship the radio operator is traditionally given a nickname, and the clue reads like a description of his off-duty cabin

explanation.surface: Where a ship's wireless operator unwinds between watches.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship's radio officer is traditionally nicknamed after the sparks of early spark-gap transmitters; the clue also hints at SPA, a place for relaxation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors' slang nickname for the wireless operator aboard a vessel.

clue.text: Some regret only attending one school

indicators.note: some means a part of the words that follow supplies the letters

explanation.surface: One regret about going to just one school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals the run inside 'regret only'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: New post quite undemanding? That's illuminating!

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: light duties are ones that are easy and undemanding

explanation.surface: Someone delighted that their latest job is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges POST into SPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage lamp that throws a strong beam onto one performer.

clue.text: Medical practitioners exercise back here

indicators.note: back tells us the run of letters is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: MOs are medical officers, doctors
PE stands for physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Doctors work out at the rear of some building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MOSPE round; 'here' is the Surrey racecourse town, linked to 17 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The bare pointer names a place: the Surrey town famous for its Derby racecourse.

clue.text: Discomfort is of little account to a man

parts.note: a/c or AC is the short form of account
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone's pain dismissed as a trifle by a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous pain is a kind of physical discomfort.

clue.text: A receptacle on certain occasions

indicators.note: occasions in the old sense of causes or brings about, here making the letters into something new

explanation.surface: A box used only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasions' rearranges ON and CERTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel or box for holding things.

clue.text: Sit near awkward characters-less agreeable

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters lie in a clumsy order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Being seated beside difficult people makes things less pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward characters' rearranges SIT and NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning unpleasant or spiteful.

clue.text: A Scot, we hear or 13 might attract him

definitions.text: A Scot, we hear or 13 might attract him

parts.words: A Scot, we hear or 13 might attract him
parts.note: a Scot spoken aloud gives the Berkshire racecourse, and 13 across is the Surrey one; both draw spectators

explanation.surface: A Scotsman or a town might lure some man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Scot, we hear' sounds like Ascot, a racecourse near Windsor; 13 across is Epsom, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes to horse races as a spectator.

clue.text: Make notes about plagiarism when scoring

indicators.note: about means the singing word goes round the copying word

parts.note: to sing is to make musical notes
a crib is something copied from another

explanation.surface: Writing about copying when marking an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CRIB inside SING.
explanation.definitionFit: Scribing is marking or scoring a line with a pointed tool.

clue.text: Climbers make them for cash

parts.note: as can mean for, in the sense of in the role of
cents are small coins, cash

explanation.surface: Mountaineers who go up peaks for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbs up mountains or slopes are what mountaineers undertake.

clue.text: Sticks up for the self-complacent

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from the bottom

parts.note: gums means sticks with glue

explanation.surface: Defending people who are pleased with themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GUMS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively pleased with oneself.

clue.text: Leather-but not for show

definitions.meaning: the skin of an animal, tanned or raw
to keep something concealed rather than display it

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is an animal's skin used for leather; as a verb it means to conceal, keep out of sight.

clue.text: Fish kept on weed

parts.note: had means kept or possessed
dock is a broad-leaved weed

explanation.surface: A fish was held in place on some weed.
explanation.definitionFit: A North Atlantic food fish related to cod.

clue.text: Beat in a thin plate

parts.note: lam means beat or thrash

explanation.surface: Hammering a slim sheet of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin layer or scale of material.

clue.text: Seeing a little notice in this place, hold on

parts.note: an ad is a short notice, an advertisement
here means this place

explanation.surface: Spotting a small sign telling you to wait right here.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick fast or cling to something.

clue.text: A plant obtainable from North American nurserymen

indicators.note: the answer can be got out of the letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A flower sold by nurseries in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtainable from' signals the letters sitting inside the words NORTH AMERICAN NURSERYMEN, spanning AMERICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather belongs to this genus of low evergreen shrubs.

clue.text: Deceitful junior employee?

definitions.meaning: split in two it is a hand, a worker, who is under others

explanation.definitionFit: Means sly or dishonest; split as under-hand it pictures a worker placed below others.

clue.text: Bars flighty creatures

definitions.meaning: rods or railings forming a barrier
flighty means able to fly; these are marsh birds

explanation.definitionFit: Horizontal bars in a fence, and also wading birds of the crake family.

clue.text: Tin-ore working in the east

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Tin mining in eastern lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges TIN and ORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is the old name for the countries of Asia, lying eastward from Europe.

clue.text: One finds many in easily-managed quarters

indicators.note: in puts the two letters within the word for easily managed

parts.note: docile means compliant and easy to manage
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single person finds plenty of people in comfortable lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: M (many) and I (one) go inside DOCILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A domicile is one's home or dwelling, the place where one lives.

clue.text: Storm back, getting in the way, to have a look

indicators.note: getting in means going inside the abbreviation for road

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

indicators.note: back means the word for storm is read from right to left

parts.note: rage means storm or fume

explanation.surface: Someone storms back obstructing the road to take a peek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAGE into EGAR, and 'getting in' puts it inside RD.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at or gaze upon, so it covers taking a look.

clue.text: A clouded picture

parts.note: clouded suggests blurred or murky, but it means a painting full of clouds

explanation.definitionFit: A painting or view of the heavens, typically with clouds.
